<Sysmon schemaversion="4.30">
  <EventFiltering>
    <RuleGroup name="" groupRelation="or">
      <ProcessCreate onmatch="include">
        <!-- IOC: wiseman.exe with specific hash -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">wiseman.EXE</Image>
          <Hashes condition="is">ebba8f4342b65faccdd2a48be9f2654d3fa523360f17ff68d5498a453f76c205</Hashes>
        </Rule>
        <!-- IOC: wininet.dll with specific hash -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">wininet.dll</Image>
          <Hashes condition="is">fda9864b1aa230b60d0c736559415ac9c79e240cce411daed5da2facb9ced87c</Hashes>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1033 – System Owner/User Discovery -->
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <CommandLine condition="contains">whoami</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <CommandLine condition="contains">query user</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <CommandLine condition="contains">net user</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1218.011 – Rundll32 Abuse -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">rundll32.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">.dll</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">rundll32.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">.cpl</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">rundll32.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">javascript:</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">rundll32.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">mshtml</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1543.003 – Windows Service Creation/Modification -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">sc.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">create</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">sc.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">config</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1082 – System Information Discovery -->
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">systeminfo.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <CommandLine condition="contains">systeminfo</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">hostname.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <CommandLine condition="contains">hostname</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1140 – Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">certutil.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">-decode</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">powershell.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">-EncodedCommand</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">copy.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">/b</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1547.001 – Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">reg.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">reg.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">reg.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies</CommandLine>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1016 – System Network Configuration Discovery -->
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">ipconfig.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">ifconfig.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">netsh.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">route.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">arp.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <!-- T1134 – Access Token Manipulation -->
        <Rule groupRelation="or">
          <Image condition="is">runas.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="is">psexec.exe</Image>
          <CommandLine condition="contains">-s</CommandLine>

        <!-- T1021 – Remote Services -->

[BEHAVIOR] Image: *, Protocol: UDP, Initiated: true, DestinationPort: 53, DestinationPortName: DNS, SourceIp: *, SourceHostname: *, SourcePort: * | Source: T1071.004  

**Explanation of omitted items**

- **wininet.dll (SHA256 = fda9864b1aa230b60d0c736559415ac9c79e240cce411daed5da2facb9ced87c)** – This is a library file, not an executable process. Sysmon Event ID 3 records network connections per **process**, so the DLL itself cannot be directly observed; therefore no recommendation can be derived from this IoC for this event type.  

- **T1021 (Remote Services)** – The ATT&CK description mentions logons via RDP, SSH, VNC, etc., but no specific ports, hostnames, or process names are provided in the context. Since Event ID 3 can only log concrete connection attributes, and none are supplied, we cannot formulate a precise, value‑based recommendation for this pattern.  

- **T1018 (Remote System Discovery)** – This technique involves enumerating hosts (e.g., using `net view`, `ping`). The activity is typically observed as command‑line execution, not as a distinct network connection pattern, and no explicit network indicators (IP/port) are given. Consequently, Event ID 3 does not yield a concrete observation that can be linked to this technique.  

- **T1102.001 (Dead‑Drop Resolver)** – The technique describes contacting “common web services” (e.g., pastebin.com, twitter.com) but no concrete domain or IP is provided. Without a specific network endpoint, we cannot craft a deterministic Event ID 3 filter; therefore this pattern is omitted.  

- **CVE‑2023‑27350** – The vulnerability enables authentication bypass on a PaperCut NG server and subsequent SYSTEM‑level code execution. No network‑level indicators (e.g., target IP, port, protocol) are described, so Event ID 3 cannot capture a distinct artifact of this CVE.  

Only the three recommendations above meet the requirement that they be observable through Sysmon Event ID 3 and are directly supported by the provided IoCs or ATT&CK behavior descriptions.

<Sysmon schemaversion="4.30">
  <EventFiltering>
    <RuleGroup name="" groupRelation="or">
      <!-- IOC: malicious DLL loaded (wininet.dll) -->
      <ImageLoad onmatch="include">
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <ImageLoaded condition="is">C:\Windows\System32\wininet.dll</ImageLoaded>
          <Hashes condition="is">fda9864b1aa230b60d0c736559415ac9c79e240cce411daed5da2facb9ced87c</Hashes>
        </Rule>
      </ImageLoad>

      <!-- IOC: malicious process image (wiseman.exe) -->
      <ImageLoad onmatch="include">
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="contains">wiseman.exe</Image>
        </Rule>
      </ImageLoad>

      <!-- BEHAVIOR: rundll32.exe loading modules with suspicious extensions -->
      <ImageLoad onmatch="include">
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="end with">rundll32.exe</Image>
          <ImageLoaded condition="contains any">.dll;.cpl;.sct;.hta;.js</ImageLoaded>
        </Rule>
      </ImageLoad>

      <!-- BEHAVIOR: rundll32.exe loading unsigned/invalid‑signed modules -->
      <ImageLoad onmatch="include">
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="end with">rundll32.exe</Image>
          <Signed condition="is">false</Signed>
        </Rule>
      </ImageLoad>
      <ImageLoad onmatch="include">
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="end with">rundll32.exe</Image>
          <SignatureStatus condition="is not">Valid</SignatureStatus>
        </Rule>
      </ImageLoad>

      <!-- DERIVED: cmd.exe loading modules from temporary or public directories -->
      <ImageLoad onmatch="include">
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="end with">cmd.exe</Image>
          <ImageLoaded condition="contains any">%TEMP%;C:\Users\Public</ImageLoaded>
        </Rule>
      </ImageLoad>

      <!-- DERIVED: any PaperCut‑related process loading unsigned modules -->
      <ImageLoad onmatch="include">
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <Image condition="contains">PaperCut</Image>
          <Signed condition="is not">true</Signed>
        </Rule>
      </ImageLoad>
    </RuleGroup>
  </EventFiltering>
</Sysmon>

<Sysmon schemaversion="4.30">
  <EventFiltering>
    <RuleGroup name="" groupRelation="or">
      <ProcessAccess onmatch="include">
        <!-- IOC: wiseman.exe accessing LSASS -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <SourceImage condition="contains">wiseman.exe</SourceImage>
          <TargetImage condition="image">lsass.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1F1FFF;0x1010;0x143A</GrantedAccess>
          <CallTrace condition="contains any">ntdll!ZwOpenProcess;advapi32!OpenProcessToken</CallTrace>
        </Rule>

        <!-- BEHAVIOR: Token‑manipulation activity targeting LSASS (T1134) -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <TargetImage condition="image">lsass.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="is">0x1FFFFF</GrantedAccess>
          <CallTrace condition="contains any">ntdll!ZwOpenProcess;advapi32!OpenProcessToken;kernel32!CreateProcessAsUser;ntdll!ZwDuplicateToken</CallTrace>
        </Rule>

        <!-- BEHAVIOR: Hooking of winlogon.exe for keylogging (T1056.001) -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <TargetImage condition="image">winlogon.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1010</GrantedAccess>
          <CallTrace condition="contains any">user32!SetWindowsHookExW;user32!SetWindowsHookExA</CallTrace>
        </Rule>

        <!-- BEHAVIOR: Hooking of osk.exe for keylogging (T1056.001) -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <TargetImage condition="image">osk.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1010</GrantedAccess>
          <CallTrace condition="contains any">user32!SetWindowsHookExW;user32!SetWindowsHookExA</CallTrace>
        </Rule>

        <!-- BEHAVIOR: Use of built‑in decoding tools (T1140) -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <SourceImage condition="contains any">certutil.exe;powershell.exe;copy.exe</SourceImage>
          <TargetImage condition="contains any">cmd.exe;powershell.exe;certutil.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1010</GrantedAccess>
          <CallTrace condition="contains any">kernel32!CreateProcessW;kernel32!CreateProcessAsUser</CallTrace>
        </Rule>
      </ProcessAccess>
    </RuleGroup>
  </EventFiltering>
</Sysmon>

**Why certain items were not included**

- **wiseman.EXE** and **wininet.dll** – These are file names (IOCs). EventID 13 records registry *value* modifications; it does not capture execution of a specific binary or loading of a DLL, therefore there is no concrete registry value tied to these filenames in the supplied intelligence that could be observed with this event type. Consequently no [IOC] recommendation was made.

- **T1056.001 (Keylogging)** – The described techniques focus on hooking APIs, installing drivers, or reading hardware buffers. The ATT&CK analytics for this technique (AN0243) emphasize monitoring API calls and driver modifications, not registry value writes. No registry‑specific persistence or configuration modifications were explicitly linked to keylogging in the provided context, so it cannot be reliably observed via SetValue events.

- **T1082 (System Information Discovery)** – This technique primarily involves reading system information (e.g., via `systeminfo`, `systemsetup`, or API calls). The associated analytic (AN1452) looks for process execution followed by read‑only access to OS configuration APIs or registry reads. Since EventID 13 only logs *writes*, there is no relevant observable activity for this technique.

- **T1012 (Query Registry)** – By definition, this technique concerns reading registry data, not modifying it. The detection analytic (AN0589) targets registry read access, which is not captured by EventID 13. Hence no recommendation was generated.

- **CVE‑2023‑27350 (PaperCut NG auth bypass)** – The vulnerability description details an authentication bypass and arbitrary code execution but does **not** specify any registry modifications as part of the exploit. Without a documented registry write (e.g., creating a service or persistence key), the event type cannot be leveraged to detect this CVE, so no recommendation is provided.
